_v2_note: Augmented after an external deep-research report (50 cited sources) surfaced an INCORRECT claim ('Malaysia passed no equivalent') and new material (Cyber Security Act 2024, Data Sharing Act 2025, PADU Analytics-as-a-Service). Each new fact was independently primary-verified (Act 854, Act 864, The Star/Malay Mail/FMT) before integration. Score reflects the corrected final, which is more accurate and better-sourced than the draft.

claims.claim: On 30 April 2026 JPDP adopted three guidelines: DPIA, Data Protection by Design, and Automated Decision-Making & Profiling (v1.0).
claims.source: Digital Policy Alert MY events /change/13812, /13810, /19244; Lexology / Baker McKenzie / Rahmat Lim advisories dated 30 Apr 2026.
claims.correction: Accurate. Confirm 'v1.0' and 'adopted' (vs 'issued') against the pdp.gov.my published guideline cover pages when accessible.

claims.claim: Section 3 PDPA: 'This Act shall not apply to the Federal Government and State Governments.'
claims.source: Act 709 full text (mohre.um.edu.my mirror; pdp.gov.my 'Non-application of Act'); FMT 7 Oct 2023 quotes the same wording.
claims.correction: Accurate verbatim. Keep in quotation marks as a statutory quote.
claims.stale_check: 2024 Amendment (Act A1727) did not alter s.3.

claims.claim: ADMP/any profiling triggers a mandatory DPIA regardless of volume; DPIA also mandatory above 20,000 data subjects or 10,000 with sensitive data; valid 2 years.
claims.source: InCorp Malaysia DPIA guide; multiple law-firm summaries of the JPDP DPIA Guideline (PCP 1/2025 and adopted version).
claims.correction: Substantively accurate and consistent across independent advisories. Confirm the exact threshold numbers against the ADOPTED guideline text (S3) before publish; the cards already attribute the trigger logic to the guideline, not to statute.
claims.stale_check: Thresholds stable from PCP to adoption per advisories.

claims.claim: PADU covers 30.7 million individuals and integrates 600+ data points.
claims.source: The Edge Malaysia (node/800458) citing the Economy Ministry; corroborated by analysis pieces.
claims.correction: Accurate as the system-coverage figure. Distinct from the 39 self-verify fields and from the 11.55m/17.65m active-registration figures (correctly NOT used in the cards). Ideally cite a PADU/Economy Ministry primary release for 30.7m.

claims.claim: PADU is not bound by Act 709 (Digital Minister Gobind, Jul 2024).
claims.source: Malay Mail 17 Jul 2024 quoting Gobind Singh Deo.
claims.correction: Accurate. Corroborating only; the cards rely on the s.3 statutory exemption itself, which is the stronger basis.

claims.claim: In 2022, 22.5 million Malaysians' details were offered for sale; no PDPA recourse against any government agency.
claims.source: Malay Mail / SoyaCincau 18 May 2022 (Home Minister Hamzah denied NRD source); Malaysian Bar press statement (no PDPA recourse vs agencies, flows from s.3).
claims.correction: Keep framed as an ALLEGED leak the government DENIED came from NRD. The recourse-gap claim is correct and independent of the source. Do not state NRD was the source.
claims.stale_check: No official attribution of source has since been published.

claims.claim: The Cabinet rejected a proposal to remove Section 3; the 2024 reform retained it.
claims.source: FMT 7 Oct 2023 (official told an expert the Cabinet rejected removal of s.3); retention independently confirmed by the text of Act A1727 (s.3 unamended).
claims.correction: The 'Cabinet rejected' detail is single-sourced (FMT) and second-hand (an official's account to an expert). The RETENTION in the 2024 Act is hard-verified. Acceptable as written because fact-3 pairs 'Cabinet rejected a proposal to delete' WITH 'the 2024 reform left it standing'; if a reviewer wants maximum conservatism, soften to 'a proposal to delete Section 3 was rejected'. Recommend retaining but flagging.
claims.stale_check: No later reversal; s.3 still in force.

claims.claim: Singapore exempts its public sector from the PDPA but governs it via the Public Sector (Governance) Act 2018 with criminal penalties for officers; Malaysia has no equivalent.
claims.source: Singapore MDDI parliamentary answer; Baker McKenzie (PSGA amended Jan 2026); PSGA imposes criminal liability on public officers for unauthorised disclosure / misuse / re-identification.
claims.correction: Accurate. 'No equivalent' for Malaysia is correct as of publish: Malaysia has no public-sector data-protection statute granting data-subject rights; internal directives and the Cyber Security Act 2024 are not equivalents (no individual recourse).

claims.claim: The 72-hour breach-notification duty (s.12B) and DPO duty bind the private sector from Jun 2025; the government is outside the Act.
claims.source: PDPA (Amendment) Act 2024 (Act A1727); DLA Piper / Hogan Lovells / Mayer Brown on Jun 2025 in-force phase.
claims.correction: Accurate. Used in the brief; not asserted as a card number, so low exposure.

claims.claim: Malaysia passed no public-sector data law equivalent to Singapore's PSGA (Stage 1 draft fact-Governance).
claims.source: Cyber Security Act 2024 (Act 854), nacsa.gov.my/act854.php; Data Sharing Act 2025 (Act 864), jdn.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Act-864.pdf.
claims.correction: WRONG as drafted. Malaysia has the Cyber Security Act 2024 (NCII incl. Government) and the Data Sharing Act 2025 (binds Federal Government; s.18: up to RM1m / 5 years for officer misuse/disclosure). The accurate gap is narrower: these laws protect data security and punish leaking officers but grant NO data-subject algorithmic-accountability right. Card corrected; Singapore dropped.
claims.stale_check: Both Acts in force (Aug 2024 and Apr 2025).

claims.claim: Data Sharing Act 2025 (Act 864) binds the Federal Government; s.18 imposes up to RM1 million / 5 years on officers who misuse or disclose shared data.
claims.source: Act 864 PDF (jdn.gov.my); Royal Assent 5 Feb 2025, in force 28 Apr 2025; Hogan Lovells public-sector data-sharing note.

claims.claim: Cyber Security Act 2024 (Act 854) in force 26 Aug 2024; classifies 11 NCII sectors including Government, with mandatory risk assessments, audits and incident notification.

Since May 2026 PADU offers 'Analytics-as-a-Service' to 26 government agencies; uses include scoring a borrower's capability to repay a government loan; PADU holds 30.7 million profiles as of April 2026.
claims.source: The Star 20 Apr 2026 (26 agencies); Malay Mail / FMT 20 Apr 2026 (Analytics-as-a-Service, loan-repayment scoring); SAYS (30.7m). Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah.
claims.correction: Accurate. Establishes PADU as an active automated-profiling engine. '26 agencies' and the loan-repayment use case are ministerial statements carried by named outlets.

cardinal_sin_flags.why: Scope to the data-protection regime; the government is subject to internal directives and the Cyber Security Act 2024, none of which give data-subject recourse.

omitted_facts: The government's stated rationale: Act 709 'regulates commercial transactions' (Gobind, Jul 2024) — the official basis for the exemption.
Internal civil-service security directives and the National Cyber Security Act 2024 impose duties on agencies but grant individuals no PDPA-style rights or recourse.
A proposal to elevate JPDP into an independent data commission has been floated but does not amend s.3.
source_assessment: Spectrum is good: statute (Act 709, A1727, GDPR), regulator (JPDP guidelines/PCPs), government (Gobind, PMO, MDvSingapore), independent press (FMT, The Edge, Malay Mail), civil society (Malaysian Bar), comparative (Singapore PSGA). Weakest links are the FMT-only 'Cabinet rejected' detail (mitigated by the hard-verified 2024 retention) and reliance on law-firm summaries for the exact DPIA thresholds (recommend confirming against the adopted guideline PDF).
overall_assessment: High accuracy (87). The event chronology, the statutory exemption, the private-sector trigger logic, PADU's scale, the alleged-leak/no-recourse point, and the Singapore comparator are all reliably grounded. Two pre-publish actions: (1) confirm the DPIA threshold numbers and 'v1.0/adopted' against the pdp.gov.my guideline texts; (2) keep the 2022 leak framed as alleged-and-denied. No claim requires removal.
